meta.title: Who really said "An artist's duty is to reflect the times"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Yes — Nina Simone really said it. On camera (c. 1969) she said “An artist's duty, as far as I'm concerned, is to reflect the times.” The meme just trims it.
meta.ogTitle: Who really said 'An artist's duty is to reflect the times'?
meta.ogDescription: Genuinely Nina Simone — from a televised interview, best known via the 2015 documentary. Her actual line kept the phrase “as far as I'm concerned.”

answer.label: Spoken by
answer.sourceLine: This one is real. Nina Simone said it on camera in a televised interview (archival footage from around 1969), the clip most people now know from the 2015 documentary What Happened, Miss Simone?. Her full line kept a qualifier the meme drops: “An artist's duty, as far as I'm concerned, is to reflect the times.”

source.excerpt: You can't help it. An artist's duty, as far as I'm concerned, is to reflect the times. I think that is true of painters, sculptors, poets, musicians… How can you be an artist and NOT reflect the times?
trail: The line is genuinely Nina Simone's — recorded footage shows her saying it in a televised interview, and the clip is featured prominently in Liz Garbus's 2015 film What Happened, Miss Simone? ↗.
Her actual wording kept a personal qualifier: the fuller form runs “You can't help it. An artist's duty, as far as I'm concerned, is to reflect the times,” as recorded on quote aggregators ↗.

Neither Wikiquote's sourced section ↗ nor Quote Investigator currently carries a dedicated entry pinning the exact broadcast; the safest sourcing is the archival interview footage itself, as circulated through the documentary.
source.excerptNote: The widely shared “An artist's duty is to reflect the times” is a trimmed version of her fuller spoken statement.

author.name: Nina Simone
author.heading: About Nina Simone
author.bio: Nina Simone, born Eunice Kathleen Waymon, was an American singer, pianist, and songwriter whose work moved freely across jazz, blues, soul, gospel, and classical music. A central artistic voice of the civil-rights movement, she wrote and performed protest songs such as Mississippi Goddam and To Be Young, Gifted and Black, and came to be called the “High Priestess of Soul.”

misattribution.heading: Real quote, trimmed wording
misattribution.intro: The attribution is right — this is genuinely Nina Simone. What travels online is a slightly edited version of what she actually said.

items.why: The meme “An artist's duty is to reflect the times” drops her qualifier. On camera she said “An artist's duty, as far as I'm concerned, is to reflect the times” — framed as a personal creed rather than a rule for everyone, per the fuller recorded quote ↗.
It is often presented as a written maxim, but it was spoken in a televised interview and is best known today through the 2015 documentary, as noted by Colorlines ↗.

misattribution.truthLine: She really said it — the key phrase is verbatim from her own recorded words; only the interjection “as far as I'm concerned” gets lost in the meme version ↗.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Simone offered this definition of the artist at the height of the U.S. civil-rights struggle, a period when she had turned her performances into acts of protest with songs like Mississippi Goddam. For her, reflecting the times was not optional decoration but the very thing that made someone an artist.
That is why the line resonates so widely today: it reframes political and social engagement as the artist's core responsibility rather than a distraction from craft.
